title: Ketia bar Shalom
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Avodah Zarah 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.10b.11-15) relates that he was a great and honored minister in the Roman government. The emperor hated the Jews; he gathered all his ministers and said to them: “If someone has an abscess on his foot, should he cut it off and live, or leave it and suffer?” They said to him: “He should cut it off and live.” Ketia bar Shalom said to them: “First, you cannot [destroy] all of them … and furthermore, they will call you a truncated kingdom.” The emperor said to Ketia: “You have spoken well; but whoever defeats the king is thrown into [a chamber filled with earth](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Avodah_Zarah.10b.14.2).” As they were taking him (to be killed), a certain noblewoman said to him: “Woe to the ship that goes without paying the tax” (you are going to be killed for Israel’s sake and you are not circumcised). Ketia bent down and cut off his foreskin, and commanded that all his property be given to Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues … A heavenly voice went out and said: “Ketia bar Shalom is destined for the life of the world to come.”[^1]
Hyman suggests that possibly he was called Ketia (“cut off”) because he defeated the king by cutting himself, and called bar Shalom because he had life in the world to come.[^2]

notes.text: Rashi explains the place of execution as a house filled with earth. The linked Davidson English renders it as a house full of ashes.

[Heilprin’s entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3040&lang=en) also records the circumcision, bequest and promise of the world to come. Hyman’s explanation of the name is his conjecture.
